title: The north star: a path to beating Minecraft like a person

brief.state:
Snapshot: the newest files are from about 2:55 PM ET, Wed 7 Oct 2026 (whole-model roadmap rev. 10-06 with 10-07 addenda, 8A spec, creative roadmap, progress board at 2:48 PM). Of the queued jobs, only B2's 6-seed confirm (PASS-1) has a result.

Own model B2 (3,302,481 trainable params, from scratch): letter reader with a +-4-letter window, a 2-block controller looped 8 rounds over 17 state vectors, an exact int64 calculator inside the forward pass, regex-fed number slots, and a copy talker. On 6 seeds it scores pooled-5 74.0 (73.0-74.7). That is +20.3 over a same-size plain transformer (53.7) and +6.9 over the step-writing transformer (67.1), ahead on 6 of 6 seeds. PASS-2 (public pretrained baselines) has not run. Weak spots: variant split 34.7% (misses about 65%); held-out family split 0.6-2.5%; the leak check (thinker off) fails on seeds 201 and 203 (10.8, 5.7 against a limit of 5); it loses to the step-writer on fewshot_number_rule and rule_apply. Its 10.9M students trained on teacher data scored about 11% on new kinds, and the teacher-variety test was proved wrong (B1-a +0.78 against +15).

Ben's targets: about 400M whole, made of EmbeddingGemma 2's text part (271M, frozen), a thinker grown to about 100M, and a talker of about 25M. Nothing above 10.9M has been trained on our data. The size ladder (8A) is sealed but not run. It uses 3.3M, 10M and 30M shapes, 6 seeds each, on the home PC, with a plain arm at each size. The first look at a deep 10M (10.25M params, 2 seeds) should read around 7 AM ET on 10-08.

Ben's design changes are not yet tested: the calculator as an outside tool (T1 screen queued, marks sealed), a learned stop (2d/H1, spec only), and more context per letter (W1, untested). Removing the window alone costs 6.3-6.8 points, so the window stays. B2 is not yet hard-code-free: its answer path still has about 17 hand-written parts (inventory A1-A17).

Creative line (B2 on the C2 rule-induction card task, DEV only): cold start failed without stepping stones; code-made stones pass the gate, but the gain is only on square and last_digit. Keeping add/mult replay stops forgetting, not the climb. Retrying stuck questions (32, then 480 more tries) gave a multi-step climb of +10.4 on s100 and +9.7 on s101 (one question short). The real test (job 9, six parents, sealed test) is training on the Mac, due about 4 PM ET.

North star: there is no code, result or ETA for a crafting world, Craftax, eyes or ears. Those are designs (C5, 12a, PR #25, PR #26), and vision and audio were paused on 10-03.

distinct.title: Mid-loop prompt cut: does B2's state keep a binding?
distinct.summary: B2 re-reads the whole prompt every round, so a binding written inside one prompt never has to be remembered. This CPU probe swaps a donor's prompt-derived inputs in at round 4 while keeping the 17 state vectors, and asks whether the state still holds the original question's value. It is the cheapest test of whether any in-state memory exists before anything is built.
distinct.change: Diagnostic script beside probe_loops.py, no model change. At round 4 replace reader output X and mask, number-slot embeddings and validity, and word keys with a donor's (same family, different answer; evalx.donor_pairs), keep Z. Fit a ridge probe on uncut round-8 states (label: last digit of the first step's first prompt-number operand, 10 classes) on train rows and score cut states against the original and the donor digit on dev in_dist. Cuts at rounds 0, 2, 4, 6; each run with executed results Rs kept and zeroed; controls: untrained same-size B2 and reader-slot ceiling.
distinct.why: Whole-state donor swaps already show the state matters (donor_match 58.2% on seed 200) but they replace the state too, so they cannot say whether Z holds the old prompt. Cutting only the prompt separates 'Z still holds the old value' from 'Z only mirrors the new prompt'. Controls 2-7 are used memory (zeroing them costs 7.8 chain-5 points), so some state use is already visible.

evidence.claim: Z starts from learned constants (ctrl.weight and place rows), so nothing carries across questions; each round cross-attends to the full prompt.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Seed 200: donor-state lesion exact 3.2%, donor_match 58.2%; zero_state 0%.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Zeroing controls 2-7 costs -1.6 pooled-5 and -7.8 chain-5 on seed 200.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Raw B2 checkpoints for confirm seeds 200-205 exist (sha-verified) in code/b2ckpt; the train and dev rows the probe needs are on the PC, not in this snapshot.

evidence.claim: Kept executed results can carry an operand's last digit, so only the Rs-zeroed variant tests Z alone.
evidence.label: suggested

test.where: PC CPU (needs custom-io/work/data and data_big copies); raw B2 seeds 200-205 from code/b2ckpt.
test.arms: Uncut vs cut at rounds 0/2/4/6; Rs kept vs zeroed; untrained control; reader ceiling. Six seeds, no screen needed.
